## Inherited audit contracts (verbatim; binding on the fill)

The rows below are quoted verbatim from the two findings tables (columns joined: number and severity, declaration, claim, evidence, proposed fix). Round 1's finding 1 and minors 2–3 were repaired in the statements you fill; their text explains the clauses you must meet.

### Round 1 (`audits/s12-8-statements-findings.md`)

> **1 (major)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean · `exists_recordStepTM`; Build/InputCall.lean · `exists_inputSeekTM`. *Claim:* The contracts are too weak for their named space-bounded consumers. *Evidence:* They bound time and restore the final tapes, but impose no bound on visited work cells. Concrete admissible detour: when the native head reads a symbol, move it left to position 0, recording one unary scratch mark per move; retrace and erase the marks while restoring the input head and scratch head. At a blank input position, skip this detour. It costs O(pos + 1), restores everything, and visits pos + 1 scratch cells. Prepending it preserves both stated time bounds. For record stepping, take the identity source machine with k = 0 and identity tag update: the detour followed by `yes` already satisfies the whole functional contract, but at pos = n its space is Θ(n), while the record length L = `posWidth n + 4` is Θ(log n). Thus restoration and O(L + n) time do not yield the O(L) workspace required by the advertised Savitch route; the analogous seek contract does not yield logspace either. *Fix:* Strengthen the same existential witnesses with trajectory/visited-set bounds through the verdict: O(L + 1) for record stepping and O(w.length + 1) for input seeking, independent of native-head travel. Prefer fixed intervals about entry heads so repeated calls compose. Re-audit the strengthened statements before fill.

> **2 (minor)** — Build/InputCall.lean · `exists_inputSeekTM` proof sketch. *Claim:* The literal existence statement is true, but its cited rewind route is off by one. *Evidence:* The statement asks for input position p, restored work tapes/heads/output, and a first exit within C·(w.length + pos + p + 1). `Simulation.lean::timed_rewind` returns to position 1, with bound pos + 2; it does not stop at position 0. For x = [false], w = [], p = 0, the sketched rewind followed by zero right moves leaves position 1. After one extra left move, copy–rewind–countdown–clear gives the claimed statement: the costs are bounded by `6*w.length + pos + 5*p + 13` with four seam dispatches, so a fixed coefficient suffices. Boundary checks: empty input/empty counter, leading-zero counters, and p = n + 1 all work. *Fix:* Insert the left move after `timed_rewind`, correct its quoted bound, and retain the finite first-exit construction. Add the space guarantee in finding 1.

> **3 (minor)** — Build/InputCall.lean · `FinTM.exists_inputCallTM` proof sketch. *Claim:* The statement is true, but the proposed inherited first-return proof lacks the callee's time-zero cut. *Evidence:* The requested module copies x from the blank seam, computes f x, and installs it on genuine tape 0 within c·(T(n) + n + (f x).length + 1), with positive return time. The copy establishes the exact entry seam of `exists_installCallTM`. However, that theorem excludes exits only at `0 < t' < t`, whereas `seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg` also needs t' = 0. A stationary identity callee with `entry = exit` and return time 1 satisfies the install-call interface, but the proposed composite visits its final exit immediately after dispatch, before the proposed total time. Split on `entry = exit`; in that branch, `seamReleaseTM_firstReturn` supplies a fresh entry before composition. Empty input/result, identity f, and a constant-output zero-work-tape source then present no obstruction; the returned module still has positive tape count. *Fix:* Add the entry/exit case split and release adapter to the sketch. Do not infer a time-zero cut from a first-positive-return contract.

> **28 (note)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean · `exists_recordStepTM` functional content. *Claim:* The functional/time statement is constructible; its missing space guarantee is separate. *Evidence:* Read the finite state/tag/scanned-cell/edge data before writing; the next configuration is outside the window exactly when a moved work head crosses an edge, so that branch can return `no` with the original record. Otherwise rewrite the scanned cells, marks, state, tag, and clamped input position; the layout length on both sides is `k*(2*s + 1) + posWidth n + k + 4`, so the in-place interval is sufficient. To satisfy arbitrary host input positions, explicitly save the original position in binary, perform the simulated read, and restore it; when n = 0, detected by the one-digit position width, the input is known blank and need not be moved. Fixed many scans and amortized counter operations give O(L + n + 1). Checks: halted c uses `outputSymbol = none` and hupd, s = 0 with an outward move takes `no`, and k = 0 only updates state/input position/tag. *Fix:* Add finding 1's bound and name the saved-input-position and clamping obligations in the construction sketch.

> **29 (note)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean · `exists_recordEqTM`. *Claim:* Empty fields do not make the equality statement false; the one-sided length bound is adequate. *Evidence:* The fixed field count k + 3 lets finite control compare exactly that many fields, counting consecutive delimiters individually rather than treating a double blank as table termination. Every successful field comparison is followed by skips; at the first failure both heads have already returned to that field's starts, and only the preceding equal fields need to be crossed back. Each failed comparison costs at most twice the current fs field length plus two, so an arbitrarily longer gs does not violate the bound. Checks: all fields empty, unequal first fields, and equal prefixes followed by a short fs field versus a very long gs field. *Fix:* Keep the stronger arbitrary-field-list contract; neither nonempty fields nor `RecordValid` is necessary.

> **30 (note)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean · `exists_recordTestTM`. *Claim:* The state/tag test needs neither a window hypothesis nor any relation between host input y and recorded input x. *Evidence:* The first and last fields contain exactly the state and tag; k + 2 forward skips, two folds, and inverse skips read them and restore the head and tape. Their total length is O(L), and finite Q/T make dispatch on P finite. Checks: k = 0, a nonwindowed c, and a completely different native input y. A constant predicate may validly use an immediate verdict; it is still a reached, correct verdict. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **32 (note)** — TuringMachine/SymbolLift.lean · complete R8.0 public surface. *Claim:* The transport statements are correctly restricted and preserve exact time and work space. *Evidence:* `decodeBool` is a partial inverse of the embedding; actions map writes and emissions, configurations map tapes/output/input while preserving state and head coordinates, and lifted transitions decode reads before applying the original table. Thus the step square commutes on lifted configurations, iteration gives `liftSymbols_runFrom`, and equal head trajectories give equal visited sets and `spaceUsed`; initialization and the computation-via-e corollary follow on encoded inputs. Checks: zero tapes, halted configurations, and arbitrary nonempty output prefixes remain covered. Mixed record tapes are not globally lifted configurations: use R1 to isolate dedicated digit tapes and put the other tapes/output prefix in its frame. Keep `liftSymbols_step` public as the useful local form. *Fix:* No transport statement change. Do not apply the run or space theorem directly to a configuration with foreign symbols on its selected tapes.

> **35 (note)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean and Build/InputCall.lean · existential quantifiers and exit clauses. *Claim:* The modules are not satisfiable by a nonterminating implementation on an admissible entry. *Evidence:* Each record contract supplies a finite t and an exact verdict configuration; for stepping, the window predicate and its negation exhaust the two implications. `yes ≠ no` makes the verdicts observable. For `inputSeek`, entry ≠ exit follows globally: choose x = [], w = [], p = 0 and an entry configuration with input position 1; the required movement forces t > 0, and then the u = 0 cut excludes equality. It does not follow from the cut alone when t = 0. Empty tag types give no admissible tagged records, but the named consumer uses inhabited `Fin 3`; constant tests or identity steps may legitimately return at time 0. The input-call row's positive tape count prevents an empty-domain fake installation. *Fix:* No extra termination hypothesis is needed. Describe the input-seek nonvacuity argument with the required witness.

### Round 2 (`audits/s12-8-statements-r2-findings.md`)

> **3 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `exists_recordStepTM`. *Claim:* The strengthened step contract is true and repairs the missing workspace guarantee. *Evidence:* The record has length \(L=k(2s+1)+\operatorname{posWidth}(n)+k+4\). Initialize a scratch counter of the position-field width, save the native position by binary counting, seek to the recorded position, read, and restore; binary carry accounting gives total time linear in native travel plus the width, with workspace linear in the width. For nonempty input, a one-step right probe distinguishes the two blank boundaries; for empty input, the one-digit width identifies that case and no native movement is needed. Finite control collects the scanned work symbols and edge flags; reject an outward head move before modifying the record, otherwise rewrite the fixed-length record and clean scratch. Checks: zero source tapes, halted source, radius zero, both clamped input boundaries, and empty input. *Fix:* No statement change. Preserve the saved-position, clamping, cleanup, and trajectory obligations in the fill.

> **4 (note)** — `Build/InputCall.lean` · `exists_inputSeekTM`. *Claim:* The strengthened seek contract is true, including its native-travel-independent head bound. *Evidence:* Copy, rewind to position 1, move left once, count down while moving the native head right, then clear scratch. The stated component bounds and four dispatches give \(t\le6\,w.length+d.inputPos.val+5p+13\), while every work head stays between its entry position minus 1 and entry position plus `w.length`. Thus one fixed coefficient satisfies both bounds. Empty counters, leading-zero counters, empty input, and \(p=n+1\) all satisfy the construction. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **5 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `exists_recordEqTM`. *Claim:* Equality remains true with empty fields and with a second record much longer than the first. *Evidence:* Compare corresponding fields; a mismatch is detected after at most the first field’s length, and only equal fields are skipped. Therefore both traversals are bounded by the first layout’s length; the crossed fields have equal lengths and can be traversed backward to restore both heads. The fixed field count prevents adjacent blanks from being mistaken for an early table end. Checks: all fields empty, first-field mismatch against an arbitrarily long field, and disagreement in the last field. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **6 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `exists_recordTestTM`. *Claim:* The strengthened test contract is true without a window hypothesis or any relationship between native input `y` and source input `x`. *Evidence:* Read the state field, cross the intervening fields, read the tag, and reverse those crossings; all work occurs within the record and its delimiters. The finite predicate determines the verdict, and the native input is unused. Checks: constant predicates, a non-windowed source configuration, and unrelated or foreign-symbol native inputs. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **7 (note)** — Four repaired contracts; `S128R2SpaceProbe` · head-range lemma; `Build/Embed`, `Build/Seam`. *Claim:* The repaired bounds imply the required workspace bounds and compose at restored entry heads. *Evidence:* A head-radius bound \(R\) gives `visitedByTapeHead d t j ⊆ Icc (d.workTapePos j − R) (d.workTapePos j + R)`, hence at most \(2R+1\) visited cells per tape and total space at most \(k(2R+1)\). Repeated calls with restored entry heads and uniformly bounded sizes remain in the same intervals; stationary dispatches add no cells. R1 preserves selected-tape visited sets and leaves unselected heads fixed. Consequently records of length \(O(S+1)\) use \(O(S+1)\) workspace per frame, and logarithmic-width seeks use logarithmic workspace; movement between frames must still be charged to the host’s bounded layout. A common coefficient can be enlarged to cover both time and radius. *Fix:* No further clause required. Consumers must intercept the verdicts; these contracts do not bound an unconnected module after its verdict time.

> **8 (note)** — `Build/InputCall.lean` · `FinTM.exists_inputCallTM`. *Claim:* The statement and corrected first-return construction are sound; this remains a time-only interface. *Evidence:* Copying native input onto tape 0 establishes the install-call entry seam. If the callee’s entry equals its exit, `seamReleaseTM_firstReturn` supplies a fresh entry without changing the positive-time run; otherwise the time-zero cut follows from inequality. This covers empty input/result, identity functions, and constant functions computed with zero source tapes, while the callable witness retains positive tape count. No small-space conclusion follows: the sketched input copy alone visits linearly many work cells. *Fix:* No space clause is needed for its advertised time-only use. A future space-preserving call requires a separately specified interface.

> **28 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `cfgRecord_inj`. *Claim:* The injectivity statement is true on configuration cores and tags. *Evidence:* Equal fields give equal states, input positions, window contents, unique marked head positions, and tags; both window hypotheses extend tape equality outside the window. Conversely, equality of those components gives identical records. Checks: zero tapes, different outputs with the same core, and differing exterior tape cells when a window hypothesis is removed—the latter shows why the hypothesis matters. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **29 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `RecordValid`, `recordValid_iff`. *Claim:* Validity is exactly the stated shape condition. *Evidence:* Forward, decode the fields of a windowed configuration. Backward, choose `List.replicate n false`, use the supplied position value, put each head at `m − s`, install the supplied window contents, and make exterior cells blank; this constructs the required witness. Checks: radius-zero singleton fields, zero or multiple marks, and an out-of-range position value. The corrected documentation properly requires external width/bound information for a uniform validator. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **31 (note)** — `SymbolLift.lean` · R8.0 public surface. *Claim:* The transport definitions and exported run, time, and space statements have the correct domain and strength. *Evidence:* Decoding inverts the embedding on digits; action/configuration lifting maps symbols while retaining state and head positions. One-step commutation gives run commutation, and identical head trajectories give equal visited sets and space. Initialization and `ComputesFunInTimeVia` follow on encoded inputs. Checks: zero tapes, halted configurations, and nonempty output prefixes. Mixed rich tapes require R1 isolation of dedicated digit tapes, rather than direct application of the globally lifted-configuration theorem. *Fix:* Keep the public one-step lemma and the stated domain restriction.

> **32 (note)** — Design O6; `SymbolLift`, `inputFoldTM`, `alphabet_reduction_spaceUsed`. *Claim:* Mandatory validation remains a sufficient and necessary safeguard for the chosen reduction interface. *Evidence:* The exported reduction requires a bound on all rich inputs, whereas lift transport controls encoded inputs. For example, a binary machine can stop after seeing blank twice, but move a work head forever if a symbol follows its first blank; binary inputs cannot exhibit the latter pattern, while `[foreign, e false]` can after decoding. A native fold rejects foreign symbols with fixed work heads; accepted inputs are encoded binary inputs. Correct consumers must also connect the repaired modules’ verdicts and final halt so their workspace bounds hold at every time. *Fix:* Retain O6 and the dedicated-digit-tape discipline.


## Gate guidance (binding; `audits/s12-8-statements-resolutions.md`)

- **The record step's obligations** (round-2 note 3, round-1 note 28): save the native input
  position in binary and restore it; seek, read, restore; clamp the position field at `0` and
  `|x| + 1`; reject an outward work-head move **before writing**; rewrite the fixed-length record;
  clean every scratch tape; keep the head-radius clause `C·(L + 1)`. `|x| = 0` is detected from
  the one-digit width and needs no native movement.
- **Intercept every verdict** (round-2 note 7). The contracts bound nothing after a module's own
  verdict or exit. Inside the record step, redirect at each sub-module's exit time (the phase
  lemma's guard is "no exit before `T`" and it dispatches at `T`); never run a sub-module past its
  exit. Consumers of your three record rows inherit the same duty.
- **R1 isolation of dedicated digit tapes** (round-1 note 32, round-2 notes 31–32). Never apply
  `liftSymbols_runFrom` or `liftSymbols_spaceUsed` to a configuration with a foreign symbol on a
  selected tape. Select only tapes 1–3, and keep them digit-only; the overlay transport
  (`liftSymbols_runFrom_over`) is the landed alternative for input-oblivious rows.
- **The input call is time-only** (round-2 note 8): add no space clause; a space-preserving call
  would be a new row.
- **The input seek** (round-1 minor 2, round-2 note 4): `timed_rewind` stops at `1`; one left move
  follows. **The input call** (round-1 minor 3): split on `entry = exit`.
- **No termination hypothesis** (round-1 note 35): each contract supplies its finite `t`.

## Known pitfalls at this pin (hard-won; most hit while building the probe)

- `rw [show (1 : ℕ) = 0 + 1 from rfl]` also rewrites the tape count of `MultiTapeTM 1 …` and the
  motive fails. Step one round with `change (M.step o).state = _` (`runFrom c 1` is `M.step c`
  definitionally).
- `simp` unfolds a machine's definition inside `counterLoopOrbit M …` arguments too, so terms
  stop matching. `generalize counterLoopOrbit M τ c r = o at …` first.
- A structure update inside `runFrom` needs an ascription:
  `({c with state := some s, inputPos := 1} : Cfg k Bool S x)`.
- `∑ r ∈ Finset.range d, τ (orbit r) + counterOverhead w (d + 1)` parses as
  `(∑ …) + counterOverhead …` (big operators bind at 67).
- `(-1 : SignType)` is `.neg` only up to unfolding: `change (moveInputPos o.inputPos SignType.neg).val = _`
  before `FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val`.
- `decide` cannot evaluate `Nat.bits`/`Nat.size`, hence `posWidth`: use `Nat.size_eq_bits_len`,
  `Nat.lt_size_self`, `Nat.lt_size`, `Nat.size_one`. `binDigits` at a literal width does decide.
- `scanTM`'s accumulator is `A : Type` and the phase types must be finite: `ScanPhase A` is
  `Fintype` from `[Fintype A]`; `phaseHostTM`'s states `Σ i, Ph i` (the family is named `Ph`,
  over `I : Type`, at `Γ : Type`) need `[Fintype I]` and `[∀ i, Fintype (Ph i)]`, and
  `DecidableEq` likewise. `FinTM` wants `State : Type`.
- `simp` rewrites `Fin.castSucc 0` to `0` and `Fin.last 1` to `1` before `Fin.lastCases_castSucc`
  (which takes `i` explicitly) can fire: after `rw [counter_cfg_eq]`, close the tape facts with
  `simp only [Fin.lastCases_castSucc, Fin.lastCases_last]`.
- `rewind_heads`/`rewind_scan_heads` are declared in `Build/Catalog.lean` but live in
  `Turing.FinTM` (beside the `f2_` family), like `timed_rewind` in `Simulation.lean`.
- The overlay transport needs a table that ignores its input (`hin`) and never writes a blank
  (`hnb`): it serves `incrementTM`/`decrementTM`, not the seek or the save loop, which read the
  input.
- `counterLoopTM M` has `k + 1` tapes with the counter at `Fin.last k`; at `k = 1` it unifies with
  the R3 rows' `2`, and `Fin.last 1 = 1` is `rfl`. At `k = 0` (the save loop) the counter is the
  only tape.
- `counterLoopCfg` ignores the body configuration's state (its state field is the host's), and
  `counterWord` freezes at zero while the machine wraps: stay at `r ≤ value + 1`.
- `embedEmitCfg`'s output is `pre ++ c.output`: start every lifted `Bool` configuration with output
  `[]` and `pre :=` the host's output, which may contain foreign symbols.
- `Cfg.inputPos : Fin (|input| + 2)`: `0` and `|input| + 1` are the clamped blanks
  (`moveInputPos`). The lifted configuration's position is `Fin.cast` of the original; compare by
  `.val`.
- A halted source has `M.step c = c` and `M.outputSymbol c = none` (`step_of_halt`,
  `outputSymbol_of_halt`).
- `seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg` needs the callee's cut at `t = 0` as well; `exists_installCallTM`
  gives it only for `0 < t`.
- `RecordAt` constrains only `[-1, |joinFields fs|]` from the head; a field's own delimiters come
  from `fieldsTape_field` and the span bound, never from cells beyond the layout.
- No `nlinarith`/`linarith` needed: `omega` with powers of two as atoms (`Nat.one_le_two_pow`,
  `pow_succ`). The linter needs a literal "Proof sketch" before every `sorry` (partial delivery
  only).

### Proof route (binding; R8 of the original brief, verbatim)

`1` = B (copy of F1: the seek target, then the F1 move scratch); `2` = Cs (the seek's blank
scratch); `3` = D (fuel counter, then the saved native position). Tapes 1–3 are **dedicated
digit tapes**: they only ever hold `RecSym.digit b` or blank. Every `Bool` row runs on them
**lifted along `e := RecSym.digitEmb Q T`**. The seek and the save loop read the native input,
so they run **R1-embedded** (`embedEmitTM ι (R.liftSymbols e)`, transported by
`embedEmitTM_runFrom` + `MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom`). Their start configuration comes from
**one single-use private lemma** derived from the public R1 API exactly as the probe's
`probeRestrict` (`embedEmitCfg_selected_tape`/`_pos`, `embedEmitTM_frame` at time `0`,
`decodeBool_apply`, `decodeBool_eq_some`): a rich host whose selected tapes hold only digits and
blanks is the R1 transport of its decoded `Bool` restriction. No general R1 reconstruction was
landed; **do not copy Primitives' private `emitterP2_frame`**. The input-oblivious,
never-blank-writing rows (`incrementTM`, `decrementTM`) may instead run lifted at the bank's own
tape count through the overlay transport `MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom_over` (with
`Cfg.liftOver`, `Cfg.decodeSymbols`, `Cfg.liftOver_decodeSymbols`), whose hypotheses `hin`, `hnb`
they meet; use one of the two transports per row, consistently. On the digit tapes,
`FinTM.bufferTape_map` and `FinTM.bufferTape_map_decode` turn delimited `Bool` words into their
lifts and back. The record tape is **never written** by a lifted row: under R1 it is never
selected, and under the overlay only the row's own digit tape changes (round-2 note 31's
isolation is what both transports provide; never apply the plain `liftSymbols_runFrom` to the
whole bank). Rich rows run on the bank directly (`scanTM 4 i`, `skipTM 4 0`, `skipBackTM 4 0`,
`copyTM`, `clearTM`). Phases, data accumulating in the phase host's index:

head, `pos ∈ {0, |x| + 1}`; one right move reads a symbol iff `pos = 0` (move back: `normal`),
else the clamp kept `|x| + 1` (move left to `|x|`: `right`). From `q₀ ≤ |x|` (`q₀ = pos`, or `|x|`
for `right`) the save body escapes at round `q₀` with the head on `0`
(`probeSaveBody_orbit`/`_exit` and the checked escape call). The fuel `2 ^ W − 1 > |x| ≥ q₀`
(`n + 1 < 2 ^ posWidth n`) keeps the escape below the counter's value. After I6 the value is

proved in the probe); `normal` decrements to `pos`, `right` seeks to `q₀ + 1 = |x| + 1 = pos`.

## Inherited audit contracts (verbatim; binding on the fill)

The rows below are quoted verbatim from the two findings tables (columns joined: number and severity, declaration, claim, evidence, proposed fix). Round 1's finding 1 and minors 2–3 were repaired in the statements you fill; their text explains the clauses you must meet.

### Round 1 (`audits/s12-8-statements-findings.md`)

> **1 (major)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean · `exists_recordStepTM`; Build/InputCall.lean · `exists_inputSeekTM`. *Claim:* The contracts are too weak for their named space-bounded consumers. *Evidence:* They bound time and restore the final tapes, but impose no bound on visited work cells. Concrete admissible detour: when the native head reads a symbol, move it left to position 0, recording one unary scratch mark per move; retrace and erase the marks while restoring the input head and scratch head. At a blank input position, skip this detour. It costs O(pos + 1), restores everything, and visits pos + 1 scratch cells. Prepending it preserves both stated time bounds. For record stepping, take the identity source machine with k = 0 and identity tag update: the detour followed by `yes` already satisfies the whole functional contract, but at pos = n its space is Θ(n), while the record length L = `posWidth n + 4` is Θ(log n). Thus restoration and O(L + n) time do not yield the O(L) workspace required by the advertised Savitch route; the analogous seek contract does not yield logspace either. *Fix:* Strengthen the same existential witnesses with trajectory/visited-set bounds through the verdict: O(L + 1) for record stepping and O(w.length + 1) for input seeking, independent of native-head travel. Prefer fixed intervals about entry heads so repeated calls compose. Re-audit the strengthened statements before fill.

> **2 (minor)** — Build/InputCall.lean · `exists_inputSeekTM` proof sketch. *Claim:* The literal existence statement is true, but its cited rewind route is off by one. *Evidence:* The statement asks for input position p, restored work tapes/heads/output, and a first exit within C·(w.length + pos + p + 1). `Simulation.lean::timed_rewind` returns to position 1, with bound pos + 2; it does not stop at position 0. For x = [false], w = [], p = 0, the sketched rewind followed by zero right moves leaves position 1. After one extra left move, copy–rewind–countdown–clear gives the claimed statement: the costs are bounded by `6*w.length + pos + 5*p + 13` with four seam dispatches, so a fixed coefficient suffices. Boundary checks: empty input/empty counter, leading-zero counters, and p = n + 1 all work. *Fix:* Insert the left move after `timed_rewind`, correct its quoted bound, and retain the finite first-exit construction. Add the space guarantee in finding 1.

> **3 (minor)** — Build/InputCall.lean · `FinTM.exists_inputCallTM` proof sketch. *Claim:* The statement is true, but the proposed inherited first-return proof lacks the callee's time-zero cut. *Evidence:* The requested module copies x from the blank seam, computes f x, and installs it on genuine tape 0 within c·(T(n) + n + (f x).length + 1), with positive return time. The copy establishes the exact entry seam of `exists_installCallTM`. However, that theorem excludes exits only at `0 < t' < t`, whereas `seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg` also needs t' = 0. A stationary identity callee with `entry = exit` and return time 1 satisfies the install-call interface, but the proposed composite visits its final exit immediately after dispatch, before the proposed total time. Split on `entry = exit`; in that branch, `seamReleaseTM_firstReturn` supplies a fresh entry before composition. Empty input/result, identity f, and a constant-output zero-work-tape source then present no obstruction; the returned module still has positive tape count. *Fix:* Add the entry/exit case split and release adapter to the sketch. Do not infer a time-zero cut from a first-positive-return contract.

> **28 (note)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean · `exists_recordStepTM` functional content. *Claim:* The functional/time statement is constructible; its missing space guarantee is separate. *Evidence:* Read the finite state/tag/scanned-cell/edge data before writing; the next configuration is outside the window exactly when a moved work head crosses an edge, so that branch can return `no` with the original record. Otherwise rewrite the scanned cells, marks, state, tag, and clamped input position; the layout length on both sides is `k*(2*s + 1) + posWidth n + k + 4`, so the in-place interval is sufficient. To satisfy arbitrary host input positions, explicitly save the original position in binary, perform the simulated read, and restore it; when n = 0, detected by the one-digit position width, the input is known blank and need not be moved. Fixed many scans and amortized counter operations give O(L + n + 1). Checks: halted c uses `outputSymbol = none` and hupd, s = 0 with an outward move takes `no`, and k = 0 only updates state/input position/tag. *Fix:* Add finding 1's bound and name the saved-input-position and clamping obligations in the construction sketch.

> **29 (note)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean · `exists_recordEqTM`. *Claim:* Empty fields do not make the equality statement false; the one-sided length bound is adequate. *Evidence:* The fixed field count k + 3 lets finite control compare exactly that many fields, counting consecutive delimiters individually rather than treating a double blank as table termination. Every successful field comparison is followed by skips; at the first failure both heads have already returned to that field's starts, and only the preceding equal fields need to be crossed back. Each failed comparison costs at most twice the current fs field length plus two, so an arbitrarily longer gs does not violate the bound. Checks: all fields empty, unequal first fields, and equal prefixes followed by a short fs field versus a very long gs field. *Fix:* Keep the stronger arbitrary-field-list contract; neither nonempty fields nor `RecordValid` is necessary.

> **30 (note)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean · `exists_recordTestTM`. *Claim:* The state/tag test needs neither a window hypothesis nor any relation between host input y and recorded input x. *Evidence:* The first and last fields contain exactly the state and tag; k + 2 forward skips, two folds, and inverse skips read them and restore the head and tape. Their total length is O(L), and finite Q/T make dispatch on P finite. Checks: k = 0, a nonwindowed c, and a completely different native input y. A constant predicate may validly use an immediate verdict; it is still a reached, correct verdict. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **32 (note)** — TuringMachine/SymbolLift.lean · complete R8.0 public surface. *Claim:* The transport statements are correctly restricted and preserve exact time and work space. *Evidence:* `decodeBool` is a partial inverse of the embedding; actions map writes and emissions, configurations map tapes/output/input while preserving state and head coordinates, and lifted transitions decode reads before applying the original table. Thus the step square commutes on lifted configurations, iteration gives `liftSymbols_runFrom`, and equal head trajectories give equal visited sets and `spaceUsed`; initialization and the computation-via-e corollary follow on encoded inputs. Checks: zero tapes, halted configurations, and arbitrary nonempty output prefixes remain covered. Mixed record tapes are not globally lifted configurations: use R1 to isolate dedicated digit tapes and put the other tapes/output prefix in its frame. Keep `liftSymbols_step` public as the useful local form. *Fix:* No transport statement change. Do not apply the run or space theorem directly to a configuration with foreign symbols on its selected tapes.

> **35 (note)** — Build/CfgRecord.lean and Build/InputCall.lean · existential quantifiers and exit clauses. *Claim:* The modules are not satisfiable by a nonterminating implementation on an admissible entry. *Evidence:* Each record contract supplies a finite t and an exact verdict configuration; for stepping, the window predicate and its negation exhaust the two implications. `yes ≠ no` makes the verdicts observable. For `inputSeek`, entry ≠ exit follows globally: choose x = [], w = [], p = 0 and an entry configuration with input position 1; the required movement forces t > 0, and then the u = 0 cut excludes equality. It does not follow from the cut alone when t = 0. Empty tag types give no admissible tagged records, but the named consumer uses inhabited `Fin 3`; constant tests or identity steps may legitimately return at time 0. The input-call row's positive tape count prevents an empty-domain fake installation. *Fix:* No extra termination hypothesis is needed. Describe the input-seek nonvacuity argument with the required witness.

### Round 2 (`audits/s12-8-statements-r2-findings.md`)

> **3 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `exists_recordStepTM`. *Claim:* The strengthened step contract is true and repairs the missing workspace guarantee. *Evidence:* The record has length \(L=k(2s+1)+\operatorname{posWidth}(n)+k+4\). Initialize a scratch counter of the position-field width, save the native position by binary counting, seek to the recorded position, read, and restore; binary carry accounting gives total time linear in native travel plus the width, with workspace linear in the width. For nonempty input, a one-step right probe distinguishes the two blank boundaries; for empty input, the one-digit width identifies that case and no native movement is needed. Finite control collects the scanned work symbols and edge flags; reject an outward head move before modifying the record, otherwise rewrite the fixed-length record and clean scratch. Checks: zero source tapes, halted source, radius zero, both clamped input boundaries, and empty input. *Fix:* No statement change. Preserve the saved-position, clamping, cleanup, and trajectory obligations in the fill.

> **4 (note)** — `Build/InputCall.lean` · `exists_inputSeekTM`. *Claim:* The strengthened seek contract is true, including its native-travel-independent head bound. *Evidence:* Copy, rewind to position 1, move left once, count down while moving the native head right, then clear scratch. The stated component bounds and four dispatches give \(t\le6\,w.length+d.inputPos.val+5p+13\), while every work head stays between its entry position minus 1 and entry position plus `w.length`. Thus one fixed coefficient satisfies both bounds. Empty counters, leading-zero counters, empty input, and \(p=n+1\) all satisfy the construction. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **5 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `exists_recordEqTM`. *Claim:* Equality remains true with empty fields and with a second record much longer than the first. *Evidence:* Compare corresponding fields; a mismatch is detected after at most the first field’s length, and only equal fields are skipped. Therefore both traversals are bounded by the first layout’s length; the crossed fields have equal lengths and can be traversed backward to restore both heads. The fixed field count prevents adjacent blanks from being mistaken for an early table end. Checks: all fields empty, first-field mismatch against an arbitrarily long field, and disagreement in the last field. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **6 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `exists_recordTestTM`. *Claim:* The strengthened test contract is true without a window hypothesis or any relationship between native input `y` and source input `x`. *Evidence:* Read the state field, cross the intervening fields, read the tag, and reverse those crossings; all work occurs within the record and its delimiters. The finite predicate determines the verdict, and the native input is unused. Checks: constant predicates, a non-windowed source configuration, and unrelated or foreign-symbol native inputs. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **7 (note)** — Four repaired contracts; `S128R2SpaceProbe` · head-range lemma; `Build/Embed`, `Build/Seam`. *Claim:* The repaired bounds imply the required workspace bounds and compose at restored entry heads. *Evidence:* A head-radius bound \(R\) gives `visitedByTapeHead d t j ⊆ Icc (d.workTapePos j − R) (d.workTapePos j + R)`, hence at most \(2R+1\) visited cells per tape and total space at most \(k(2R+1)\). Repeated calls with restored entry heads and uniformly bounded sizes remain in the same intervals; stationary dispatches add no cells. R1 preserves selected-tape visited sets and leaves unselected heads fixed. Consequently records of length \(O(S+1)\) use \(O(S+1)\) workspace per frame, and logarithmic-width seeks use logarithmic workspace; movement between frames must still be charged to the host’s bounded layout. A common coefficient can be enlarged to cover both time and radius. *Fix:* No further clause required. Consumers must intercept the verdicts; these contracts do not bound an unconnected module after its verdict time.

> **8 (note)** — `Build/InputCall.lean` · `FinTM.exists_inputCallTM`. *Claim:* The statement and corrected first-return construction are sound; this remains a time-only interface. *Evidence:* Copying native input onto tape 0 establishes the install-call entry seam. If the callee’s entry equals its exit, `seamReleaseTM_firstReturn` supplies a fresh entry without changing the positive-time run; otherwise the time-zero cut follows from inequality. This covers empty input/result, identity functions, and constant functions computed with zero source tapes, while the callable witness retains positive tape count. No small-space conclusion follows: the sketched input copy alone visits linearly many work cells. *Fix:* No space clause is needed for its advertised time-only use. A future space-preserving call requires a separately specified interface.

> **28 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `cfgRecord_inj`. *Claim:* The injectivity statement is true on configuration cores and tags. *Evidence:* Equal fields give equal states, input positions, window contents, unique marked head positions, and tags; both window hypotheses extend tape equality outside the window. Checks: zero tapes, different outputs with the same core, and differing exterior tape cells when a window hypothesis is removed—the latter shows why the hypothesis matters. *Fix:* No statement change.

> **29 (note)** — `Build/CfgRecord.lean` · `RecordValid`, `recordValid_iff`. *Claim:* Validity is exactly the stated shape condition. *Evidence:* Forward, decode the fields of a windowed configuration. Backward, choose `List.replicate n false`, use the supplied position value, put each head at `m − s`, install the supplied window contents, and make exterior cells blank; this constructs the required witness. Checks: radius-zero singleton fields, zero or multiple marks, and an out-of-range position value. > **31 (note)** — `SymbolLift.lean` · R8.0 public surface. *Claim:* The transport definitions and exported run, time, and space statements have the correct domain and strength. *Evidence:* Decoding inverts the embedding on digits; action/configuration lifting maps symbols while retaining state and head positions. ## Gate guidance (binding; `audits/s12-8-statements-resolutions.md`)

- **The record step's obligations** (round-2 note 3, round-1 note 28): save the native input
  position in binary and restore it; seek, read, restore; clamp the position field at `0` and
  `|x| + 1`; reject an outward work-head move **before writing**; rewrite the fixed-length record;
  clean every scratch tape; keep the head-radius clause `C·(L + 1)`. `|x| = 0` is detected from
  the one-digit width and needs no native movement.
- **Intercept every verdict** (round-2 note 7). The contracts bound nothing after a module's own
  verdict or exit. Inside the record step, redirect at each sub-module's exit time (the phase
  lemma's guard is "no exit before `T`" and it dispatches at `T`); never run a sub-module past its
  exit. Consumers of your three record rows inherit the same duty.
- **R1 isolation of dedicated digit tapes** (round-1 note 32, round-2 notes 31–32). Never apply
  `liftSymbols_runFrom` or `liftSymbols_spaceUsed` to a configuration with a foreign symbol on a
  selected tape. Select only tapes 1–3, and keep them digit-only; the overlay transport
  (`liftSymbols_runFrom_over`) is the landed alternative for input-oblivious rows.
- **The input call is time-only** (round-2 note 8): add no space clause; a space-preserving call
  would be a new row.
- **The input seek** (round-1 minor 2, round-2 note 4): `timed_rewind` stops at `1`; one left move
  follows. **The input call** (round-1 minor 3): split on `entry = exit`.
- **No termination hypothesis** (round-1 note 35): each contract supplies its finite `t`.

- [ ] 1/1, or the partial frontier (rule 9); the base hash and the ancestor check.
- [ ] Every new declaration with its role:
  - the step's `phaseHostTM` index and phase family;
  - the restriction lemma;
  - the Probe/Save/Read tables (rule 10), with their gap sentences;
  - the pure digit and window lemmas.
- [ ] Imports unchanged (any Mathlib addition flagged); requested shared rows; escalations,
      or "none"; appendices and status updates, each flagged.
- [ ] Duplication: both screens, before and after; every new pair justified; "new copies:
      none".
- [ ] `CfgRecord`'s size; the final sweep tail; the re-run probe; seven axiom prints, with no
      `sorryAx`; the lint line. The diff touches only `CfgRecord.lean`.

## Known pitfalls at this pin (hard-won; most hit while building the probe)

- `rw [show (1 : ℕ) = 0 + 1 from rfl]` also rewrites the tape count of `MultiTapeTM 1 …` and the
  motive fails. Step one round with `change (M.step o).state = _` (`runFrom c 1` is `M.step c`
  definitionally).
- `simp` unfolds a machine's definition inside `counterLoopOrbit M …` arguments too, so terms
  stop matching. `generalize counterLoopOrbit M τ c r = o at …` first.
- A structure update inside `runFrom` needs an ascription:
  `({c with state := some s, inputPos := 1} : Cfg k Bool S x)`.
- `∑ r ∈ Finset.range d, τ (orbit r) + counterOverhead w (d + 1)` parses as
  `(∑ …) + counterOverhead …` (big operators bind at 67).
- `(-1 : SignType)` is `.neg` only up to unfolding: `change (moveInputPos o.inputPos SignType.neg).val = _`
  before `FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val`.
- `decide` cannot evaluate `Nat.bits`/`Nat.size`, hence `posWidth`: use `Nat.size_eq_bits_len`,
  `Nat.lt_size_self`, `Nat.lt_size`, `Nat.size_one`. `binDigits` at a literal width does decide.
- `scanTM`'s accumulator is `A : Type` and the phase types must be finite: `ScanPhase A` is
  `Fintype` from `[Fintype A]`; `phaseHostTM`'s states `Σ i, Ph i` (the family is named `Ph`,
  over `I : Type`, at `Γ : Type`) need `[Fintype I]` and `[∀ i, Fintype (Ph i)]`, and
  `DecidableEq` likewise. `FinTM` wants `State : Type`.
- `simp` rewrites `Fin.castSucc 0` to `0` and `Fin.last 1` to `1` before `Fin.lastCases_castSucc`
  (which takes `i` explicitly) can fire: after `rw [counter_cfg_eq]`, close the tape facts with
  `simp only [Fin.lastCases_castSucc, Fin.lastCases_last]`.
- `rewind_heads`/`rewind_scan_heads` are declared in `Build/Catalog.lean` but live in
  `Turing.FinTM` (beside the `f2_` family), like `timed_rewind` in `Simulation.lean`.
- The overlay transport needs a table that ignores its input (`hin`) and never writes a blank
  (`hnb`): it serves `incrementTM`/`decrementTM`, not the seek or the save loop, which read the
  input.
- `counterLoopTM M` has `k + 1` tapes with the counter at `Fin.last k`; at `k = 1` it unifies with
  the R3 rows' `2`, and `Fin.last 1 = 1` is `rfl`. At `k = 0` (the save loop) the counter is the
  only tape.
- Since R8.0b, `counterLoopCfg`, `counterLoopOrbit` and `counterLoop_time_le` take the tape
  alphabet as a parameter. Typed arguments fix it at `Bool`; a positional `@` application gains
  one argument.
- `counterLoopCfg` ignores the body configuration's state (its state field is the host's), and
  `counterWord` freezes at zero while the machine wraps: stay at `r ≤ value + 1`.
- `embedEmitCfg`'s output is `pre ++ c.output`: start every lifted `Bool` configuration with output
  `[]` and `pre :=` the host's output, which may contain foreign symbols.
- `Cfg.inputPos : Fin (|input| + 2)`: `0` and `|input| + 1` are the clamped blanks
  (`moveInputPos`). The lifted configuration's position is `Fin.cast` of the original; compare by
  `.val`.
- A halted source has `M.step c = c` and `M.outputSymbol c = none` (`step_of_halt`,
  `outputSymbol_of_halt`).
- `seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg` needs the callee's cut at `t = 0` as well; `exists_installCallTM`
  gives it only for `0 < t`.
- `RecordAt` constrains only `[-1, |joinFields fs|]` from the head; a field's own delimiters come
  from `fieldsTape_field` and the span bound, never from cells beyond the layout.
- No `nlinarith`/`linarith` needed: `omega` with powers of two as atoms (`Nat.one_le_two_pow`,
  `pow_succ`). The linter needs a literal "Proof sketch" before every `sorry` (partial delivery
  only).

## Proof routes

| Contract | Route | Forward family | Return family | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `writeConstTM_run_ofCfg` | `scan_const_trace` applies public `catalog_trace_run`, length `w₀.length` | `scanConstF`: written prefix, `.wr` counter | `scanConstR`: full written word, `.bk` counter, head offset `r` | `scanConstD`: `.done`, full overwrite, restored heads |
| `writeAdvTM_run_ofCfg` | `scan_adv_run`: one forward induction through `w₀.length`, then one stationary step | `scanAdvF`: written prefix, state equal to written-cell count | none | state `0`, head advanced by `w₀.length` |
| `inputCopyTM_run_ofCfg` | `scan_copy_trace` applies public `catalog_trace_run`, length `x.length` | `scanCopyF`: shared prefix, `.sweep`, input at `r+1` | `scanCopyR`: full copy, `.rewind`, input at `r`, work offset `r−1` | `scanCopyD`: `.done`, full copy, both heads restored |
| `inputFoldTM_run_ofCfg` | `scan_fold_trace` applies public `catalog_trace_run`, length `x.length` | `scanFoldF`: fold of `x.take r`, input at `r+1` | `scanFoldR`: full fold, input at `r` | literal `{ d with state := some (.done (x.foldl δ a₀)) }` |

All finite-state indices and native-input positions use `min` to make the families total. The constant-writer and copier exit definitions use their forward family's final tape map, definitionally equal to the target's finish.

The advancing writer is cyclic. Its exit `0` is also its entry; for a nonempty word the next step writes again. Thus the stationary-exit hypothesis of `catalog_trace_run` is unavailable, and the single forward induction is necessary. No other induction was introduced.

The three writing rows share `scanWriteCfg` and `scan_write_step`. The latter cites `step_of_tapeAction_write`, and its sole written-cell argument cites `catalog_write_take`. None of the three consumers proves a one-cell overwrite again.

| Routine | Forward | Turn | Return | Entry | Exit stationarity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Constant writer | `scan_write_step` | `step_of_inputMoveAction` | `step_of_tapeAction_move` | `step_of_inputMoveAction` | `step_of_inputMoveAction` |
| Advancing writer | `scan_write_step` | final `step_of_inputMoveAction` returning to `0` | — | — | not asserted |
| Input copy | `scan_write_step` | `step_of_tapeAction_move` | `step_of_tapeAction_move` | `step_of_tapeAction_move` | `step_of_inputMoveAction` |
| Input fold | `step_of_inputMoveAction` | `step_of_inputMoveAction` | `step_of_inputMoveAction` | `step_of_inputMoveAction` | `step_of_inputMoveAction` |

Input reads cite generic `inputSymbolInner` or compute an end-marker read from `Cfg.inputSymbol`. Input movement cites `moveInputPos_zero`, `moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right`, or `FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val`. The fold's accumulator step uses `List.take_succ`, `List.getElem?_eq_getElem`, and `List.foldl_append`.

The final clauses are consequences of the instantiated public trace (or the bounded forward run): exact finish, no early exit, and every head's trajectory. The proof covers empty words/input, arbitrary nonblank frames, negative head coordinates, arbitrary alphabets, and zero work tapes for the fold. The copier's return is guided only by the input; the fold fixes every work head throughout.

The prescribed 74-module bootstrap encountered one process-level `Bus error` (exit 135) in unchanged `CodeFormat.lean` while a cache refresh was active, without an elaboration diagnostic. Compiled dependency files were isolated from other local work, and the same module then passed without source changes; the bootstrap continued in order. The final sweep is the authoritative complete verification log.

This environment needs a narrow startup compatibility shim: Lean's `/proc/<its-pid>/exe` lookup is redirected to `/proc/self/exe`, with all other `readlink` calls unchanged. Its source is included as `evidence/lean-self-path.c`. It does not modify Lean, the proof checker, or diagnostics. A normal Lean installation should not need it. To reproduce here, compile it with `cc -shared -fPIC evidence/lean-self-path.c -ldl -o /tmp/s128-lean-self-path.so` and set `LD_PRELOAD` to that absolute path while running the campaign script.

## Construction and obligations

- **Pure records:** one shared binary-value/injectivity pair. Field equality determines the core; exterior cells use both window hypotheses. Reverse validity constructs the window on `List.replicate n false`, including the unique mark and bounded native position. Neither result identifies output tapes.
- **Input seek:** exactly the prescribed copy → rewind → countdown → clear seam composition. `FinTM.rewind_heads` supplies the rewind and all work-head prefixes; `FinTM.controlAction_apply` supplies the final left step. `counter_cfg_eq` supplies the counter layout. The private one-step body uses `step_of_inputMoveAction`. The coefficient is 13 for time and radius. Every work head lies in its entry interval `[head − 1, head + |w|]`; native travel does not enlarge this interval. The finish restores tapes, work heads, and output and sets the native position to `p`. The proof's quantifiers include the empty word/input, leading-zero counters, and the rightmost clamped position.
- **Input call:** copy into the canonical argument seam and use `exists_installCallTM`; split `entry = exit`, using `seamReleaseTM_firstReturn` in that branch. The full callee cut includes time zero. Coefficient `b + 3`; this row remains time-only.
- **Test:** one public `phaseHostTM` instance. State fold with `Option (Option Q)`, `k + 2` forward skips, tag fold with `Option Bool`, and reverse skips. It explicitly invokes `phaseHostTM_run` for each kind of phase and inducts over the finite counter. Time coefficient `6 * (2 * (k + 2) + 2)`; the stronger common head radius is `L + 1`. Native input, output, tape, and entry head are restored. No window hypothesis or relationship between source and native input is assumed.
- **Equality:** one public `phaseHostTM` instance, two tapes and no scratch. Each framed compare precedes any skip; only equal fields are crossed. A mismatch returns over the equal prefix. Both return traversals are charged to the first layout, and the compare radius uses its common-prefix length, at most the first field's length. Time coefficient `12 * (2 * k + 5)`; the stronger common head radius is `L + 1`. Empty fields, an arbitrarily long mismatching second field, and arbitrary cells beyond either layout are included.
- **Shared layer:** record phases invoke the public phase lemma. `RecordRun` helpers only package endpoints/cuts/radii and concatenate established runs by `runFrom_add`; they define no host and repeat no host proof. Record framing calls `fieldsTape_field` and the public offset/span facts directly. There is no private field-layout, rewind-heads, counter-layout, buffer-map, or symbol-decoding equivalent.

## Continuation frontier

Only `exists_recordStepTM` remains. Its original body is still `by sorry`, and its original detailed proof sketch remains in the owned file. A successor should follow R8 in the brief without widening the modulo set:

1. Use one phase host on the four-tape bank: record 0, dedicated digit tapes B=1, Cs=2, D=3.
2. Read state, position flags, marked work cells and edge flags, and tag using the cited folds/copy/skips; rewind the record head.
3. Implement the permitted Probe/Save/Read native-head tables. Save the host native position using the lifted fuel countdown, complement it, and distinguish normal/right-boundary restoration. Empty native input needs no movement. Cite the public buffer mapping/decoding facts and use the single allowed R1 restriction lemma, without copying `emitterP2_frame`.
4. Seek to the recorded position, read, restore the saved native position, and clear D. Reuse the completed `exists_inputSeekTM`.
5. Reject an outward work-head move before any record rewrite. Otherwise rewrite fixed-length fields, clamp the position at 0 and `|x| + 1`, shift marks, clear scratch, and return to the entry heads.
6. Finish time `C * (L + |x| + 1)`, every-prefix work radius `C * (L + 1)`, exact restoration/cleanup, and the full verdict cut. The shared binary decoding helpers and segment bookkeeping are available; none introduces an admission.

## ===== audits/s12-8-fill-agent-reports/C-cont-1-REPORT.md =====

# Stream C continuation: checked partial, ground rule 9

The remaining public target is **not proved**. Its body now instantiates the concrete four-tape phase host and verifies its entry state-fold segment. The one direct `sorry` is the complete remaining run-contract obligation. No new private helper is admitted, and the target is not proved modulo private helpers. The proved-modulo dependency set remains empty.

Base: `4aafe9e41a5a8c9850bbfdfdc9a34a105ed26b9d`, from `complexity/arora-barak-ch3-4`; local working branch `fill/s128-C-cont`. The required ancestor `8e9a9b7eef75941a83ce036a195795c784758763` passed before implementation. The base does not include PR #38 (`be1b7691` is not an ancestor); all counter-loop use is the Bool API. No push or PR. No rebase.

Only `TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/CfgRecord.lean` changes. All original definitions and proofs, the six completed targets, all seven target signatures, all existing private declarations, imports and module status text remain unchanged. The target's original docstring is retained and receives one flagged **Fill-C continuation sketch appendix (partial)**. The new code has no axioms, unsafe definitions, native decision proofs, private admissions, private host, private field-layout lemma, private buffer-map lemma, private rewind proof, or private counter-layout lemma.

## Construction and proved components

The concrete machine uses one `phaseHostTM`, exactly four work tapes, record 0, B 1, Cs 2 and D 3. Its finite data holds source state, width/zero flags, marked symbols, edge flags, tag, native-right flag and input symbol. Its row family and redirects encode every prescribed R8 phase, including separate halt and empty-input branches, rejection before a record write, F1 clamping, tape-cell write/mark-shift passes, and cleanup/return stages. The only hand tables are Probe, Save and Read, each documenting the missing public native-input-head primitive and proved through `step_of_inputMoveAction`.

The construction is typechecked; **its complete correctness is not established**. In particular the numerical witness `200 * (k + 3) * (Cseek + 1)` is a proposed bound, not a completed ledger proof.

Completed proofs include width-one iff empty input; fixed-width carry/borrow; complement-value arithmetic and canonical saved digits; the exact outward-head/window equivalence; the single-use restriction-to-digit-bank lemma and all-prefix R1 transport wrapper; the native-table frame, read exit, save orbit, probe behavior/cut, and counter-loop escape with counter-head interval, exact endpoint, time bound and saved value; position and tape-field folds; the precise F1 clamp; point writing and mark-shift identities; and the complete pure tape-word rewrite to the field of `Action.apply`. The first state-read phase has an exact five-step `RecordRun`, full verdict cut and radius one, and is instantiated from the input `RecordAt` hypothesis inside the target body.

No mathematical obstruction or statement repair was found. Mathematical escalations: **none**. New shared rows requested: **none**; the inherited native-input-head primitive request remains an upstream opportunity. The scope and route were not widened.

## Continuation frontier

1. **Host construction complete.** Reuse `RecordStepStage`, `RecordStepData`, `recordStepPhase`, `recordStepRows`, `recordStepNext` and `recordStepMachine`. Do not introduce a second host. The digit embedding choice is consistently R1, including carry and borrow.
2. **Finish the read run R1–R6.** `recordStep_state_run` is the first segment; `hread` in the target already applies it to the input. Apply `phaseHostTM_run` to the state skip, position fold, two framed copies, position skip, tape fold/skip iterations, tag fold and `k+2` reverse skips. The pure folds are `recordStep_position_fold` and `recordStep_tape_fold`; use the existing binary value decoder and `recordStep_width_one` to identify their flags. The public `fieldsTape_field`, span and offset lemmas provide framing. Prove the accumulated data equals the source configuration/tag and B/D hold the recorded digits, with Cs blank. The prefix invariant for the tape fold is already proved.
3. **Transport the native cycle I0–I9.** The standalone Probe/Save/Read contracts and save counter arithmetic are complete. Instantiate `recordStep_transport` on `recordStepSeekBank false/true` and `recordStepDigitBank 2`, using `bufferTape_map` and `_map_decode` for the decoded starts. No phase-host native cycle has yet been concatenated. Supply the digit-only invariant, exact arbitrary output prefix restoration, all seek cuts, all nonselected tape frames, and scratch heads. On nonempty inputs, the probe gives q0=pos or q0=n; the save escapes after q0+1 decrements, complement gives q0+1, and only the normal branch borrows once before restoration. Prove the all-one fuel value and its strict reserve from `record_pos_lt`. Handle halt by clearing B/D and `hupd`, and empty input by clearing D with no native motion.
4. **Finish dispatch and rewriting A0–A5.** Connect the accumulated edge flags to `recordStep_window`, rejecting before modifying tape 0. The pure arithmetic `recordStep_position_digits` and `recordStep_tape_word` supply the exact fixed-width rewritten fields. Instantiate public map/shift, increment/decrement, copy, clear and skip contracts; prove field-by-field equality with `cfgRecord s (M.step c) (upd τ (M.outputSymbol c))` and frame every nonrecord cell.
5. **Close the common ledger.** Reuse the inherited `RecordRun`, `recordRun_tagged` and `recordRun_trans`. Account for every one-step host dispatch. Prove exact native position/output/head restoration, global blankness of B/Cs/D, the full no-verdict-before-time cut, time `C * (L + |x| + 1)` and radius `C * (L + 1)`. With the supplied generous C both estimates should follow from the field spans and seek radius, but this has not been formalized.

The sole admission is at the end of `exists_recordStepTM`, after `hread`. All these composition obligations remain inside that goal; no statement of any missing helper was postulated. The six previously completed targets remain admission-free. This is **0/1 new public targets completed**, with a proved component frontier, not a complete fill.

## Environment and verification method

Stock Lean 4.25.0 and pinned dependencies. Every Lean check used the repository's unmodified `scripts/lean_check_tree.sh`; no `lake build` was run. The sandbox's executable-path lookup required the already available launcher that supplies the installed Lean executable path via a readlink compatibility shim; it does not modify the Lean compiler, elaborator or kernel. Dependency cache retrieval used `lake exe cache get`/`get!`; after a broad cache request exhausted scratch storage, only regenerable compiled package cache entries were pruned and the 41 required Mathlib roots were fetched successfully.

There are 51 explicit new declarations: the following 48 named declarations and three private instances. Derived constructors and instances remain private with their parent types. None is admitted.

| Declaration | Kind | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `recordStep_width_one` | theorem | Detect empty input from the one-digit position width. |
| `recordStep_complement_value` | theorem | Value sum for a word and its bitwise complement. |
| `recordStep_word_of_value` | theorem | Normalize any fixed-width digit word using the existing record decoder and Mathlib digit injectivity. |
| `recordStep_digits_succ` | theorem | Simultaneous representable fixed-width carry and borrow identities. |
| `recordStep_saved_digits` | theorem | Identify complemented residual all-one fuel as the canonical word for q+1. |
| `recordStep_window` | theorem | Exact outward-head-move characterization of the applied configuration's window predicate. |
| `recordStep_restrict` | theorem | The one permitted, single-use R1 digit-bank reconstruction, from selected-tape/position and time-zero frame APIs. |
| `recordStep_transport` | theorem | All-prefix embedded symbol-lift transport, preserving an arbitrary rich frame and output prefix. |
| `recordStep_native_frame` | theorem | One shared work-bank/output preservation induction for the permitted input-only tables. |
| `RecordStepProbe` | inductive | Finite Probe control type: start, peek, and Boolean verdict. |
| `recordStepProbe` | def | Permitted input-head boundary probe; its docstring identifies the missing public native-input-head primitive. |
| `recordStepSave` | def | Permitted zero-work-tape save-loop body: a symbol moves left; a blank exits. |
| `recordStepRead` | def | Permitted stationary native-symbol decoder into finite control. |
| `recordStep_read_run` | theorem | Exact one-step Read exit and complete exit cut. |
| `recordStep_save_orbit` | theorem | Save body orbit, left-boundary escape, exact position and output. |
| `recordStep_input_blank` | theorem | A blank native cell is exactly one of the two clamped boundaries. |
| `recordStep_probe_run` | theorem | Probe's one/two-step exit, cut, right-boundary classification, resulting native position and fixed work bank. |
| `recordStep_save_run` | theorem | Public counter-loop escape specialized to Save: exact result, both exit cuts, head interval, linear time, and complementary saved value. |
| `RecordStepData` | structure | Finite nine-component data accumulator, with optional tag for potentially empty tag types. |
| `RecordStepStage` | inductive | Finite read, native-cycle, reject, rewrite, return and verdict stages. |
| `RecordStepIndex` | abbrev | Stage paired with accumulated finite data. |
| `recordStepTapeFold` | def | Read accumulator for marked content and left/right edge flags. |
| `recordStep_tape_prefix` | theorem | Single-mark field prefix invariant for that accumulator. |
| `recordStep_tape_fold` | theorem | Full tape-field scan yields the source symbol and exactly its two boundary flags. |
| `recordStepPosFold` | def | Saturating width count and all-zero flag. |
| `recordStep_position_fold` | theorem | Position scan yields min(2,width) and the represented-value-zero test. |
| `recordStepAction` | def | Source action selected from the finite read data, with an unused halted fallback. |
| `recordStepOutside` | def | Finite outward-move test before any record write. |
| `recordStepSeekBank` | def | Select B/Cs for recorded seek or D/Cs for restore; record tape 0 is excluded. |
| `recordStepDigitBank` | def | Select one of the three dedicated digit tapes for save/carry/borrow. |
| `recordStepGetMark` | def | Mark projection for the public delay transducer. |
| `recordStepSetMark` | def | Replace only the mark track. |
| `recordStepWriteCell` | def | Write only at the old marked cell. |
| `recordStep_right_clamp` | theorem | Identify the right input boundary from blankness and nonzero position. |
| `recordStep_position_digits` | theorem | F1's unchanged/carry/borrow branch equals the digits of moveInputPos. |
| `recordStep_cell_write` | theorem | Pointwise marked write equals Action.apply's tape update. |
| `recordStep_cell_shift` | theorem | Public left/right shifts and identity scan produce the exactly moved mark. |
| `recordStep_tape_word` | theorem | The two scan results form precisely the applied action's tape field. |
| `recordStepPhase` | def | Dependent row state family for the single phase host. |
| `recordStepRows` | def | Concrete library-row family on four tapes; all Bool rows use R1 only on digit selections. |
| `recordStepApply` | def | Choose reject cleanup or state rewrite after the outward-move test. |
| `recordStepFirstTape` | def | Enter the first tape field, or the tag when k=0. |
| `recordStepNext` | def | All phase exits and stationary dispatches, including finite field/backward counters and fixed verdict anchors. |
| `RecordStepControl` | abbrev | Sigma control type of the public phase host. |
| `recordStepEntry` | def | Start at the state-fold phase with empty accumulated data. |
| `recordStepVerdict` | def | Two data-independent verdict anchors. |
| `recordStepMachine` | def | Exactly one phaseHostTM instance with the prescribed family and redirects. |
| `recordStep_state_run` | theorem | Five-step first read/dispatch segment as the inherited RecordRun, with radius one and full verdict cut. |
| `Fintype (RecordStepData k Q T)` | private instance | Finite data record; local `synthInstance.maxSize 2048` accommodates the derived product instance. |
| `Fintype (recordStepPhase i)` | private instance | Finiteness of every row state type. |
| `DecidableEq (recordStepPhase i)` | private instance | Equality for every row state type. |

The restriction lemma occurs once as a declaration and once as a call, inside the reusable transport wrapper. The fixed-width predecessor proof cites `counterWord_value`, `counterWord_length`, `recordStep_word_of_value`, `record_digits_value` and the inherited `record_digits_inj`. Its only induction is the carry/borrow inverse on arbitrary lists.

## What is proved

Here `W` is the copied position-word length, `L` is the joined record length, `k` is the source work-tape count, and `Cseek` is the public seek coefficient.

- **R1–R6 complete:** `recordStep_read_all` starts at the actual entry configuration and reaches the exact source observations and tag, with canonical position digits on B and D, unchanged record/output/native position, and restored work heads. Its time is at most `(10*(k+3)+17)*(L+1)` and its radius is `L+1`. The prefix is exactly `6*W+17` steps. The tape-field loop includes `k=0`; the tag and all `k+2` reverse skips are included.
- **Halted-source branch complete inside the target:** both buffers are cleared, yes is reached, the record is unchanged by `step_of_halt`, `outputSymbol_of_halt` and `hupd`, and the full entry-to-verdict cut, exact endpoint, time and radius are proved using the existing coefficient `200*(k+3)*(Cseek+1)`.
- **I0 empty-input segment:** a live width-one read exit clears D and enters dispatch with input `none`, without native movement. This segment is proved; its use in the whole live branch remains to be assembled.
- **Rich native transports:** the public seek contract is transported to an arbitrary selected two-tape digit bank. Save is transported specifically to D, with exact residual fuel, native position zero, both exit cuts, restored heads, width-only radius, and every nonselected rich frame cell and output preserved.
- **I1–I3 composed:** fuel map, native probe and Save are connected through the existing host, including all three dispatches. The endpoint is the recorded-seek stage, input at zero, and D contains `counterWord (replicate W true) (q+1)`. The returned flag is `decide (entryInputPos = |x|+1)` and `q` is `|x|` on that branch or the original input position otherwise, with `q ≤ |x|`. Time is at most `6*W+5*|x|+12`; radius is `W+1`.
- **I4–I5 composed:** the recorded seek and Read are connected through the host, ending at complement with `input = c.inputSymbol`. D and the rich record frame are preserved, and Cs is restored by the public seek contract. Time is at most `Cseek*(W+entryInputPos+c.inputPos+1)+3`; radius is `Cseek*(W+1)`. This segment and I1–I3 are separately proved, not yet concatenated with the remainder of the native cycle in the target.
- **Rejection cleanup segment:** when the outside test is true, B is cleared and no is reached in `2*W+3` steps, with unchanged record/native components and radius `W+1`. Connecting the source window hypothesis to this test in the whole live branch remains open.

The 20 new declarations are three private definitions and 17 private theorems. The private-axiom check inspects all 20 imported declarations and rejects `sorryAx`; it passes. The proposed common coefficient is established for the halted branch only; the live-source ledger is still open.

## Exact continuation frontier

1. Reuse `hread` in the target: it now is the entire `recordStep_read_all`, not just the first state fold. `data` is `{recordStepReadData s c k with tag := some τ}`; `w` is the canonical rich position word. The `halted` branch is closed. The sole admission is the following live branch.
2. Split empty/nonempty using `recordStep_width_one`. On empty input use `recordStep_empty_run` and identify `c.inputSymbol = none`. On nonempty input instantiate `recordStep_prepare_native` with the Bool position digits; their length is `posWidth |x|`, and `record_pos_lt` gives the strict reserve. Then instantiate `recordStep_seek_read` using `hseek` at the source input position, `record_digits_value`, and the unchanged global blankness of Cs. Widen the segment radii before concatenating.
3. Complete **I6–I9**. Use `recordStep_map_snapshot` and the inherited `recordStep_saved_digits` to identify complemented D as `binDigits W (q+1)`. On the normal branch transport `decrementTM_run_succ_ofCfg` through the existing R1 wrapper on `recordStepDigitBank 2`, using `recordStep_digits_succ`; on the right-boundary branch skip decrement. Apply `recordStep_seek_transport` on `recordStepSeekBank true` with the saved original native position. Intercept its finish, clear D using the shared specialization and enter `recordStepApply`. Prove exact original native position and output restoration, plus global blank Cs/D.
4. Complete **A0–A5**. Identify `recordStepAction` from the accumulated observations, and relate `recordStepOutside` to `recordStep_window`. Use `recordStep_reject_run` on the outward branch before any record write. Otherwise instantiate the public state/tag map, F1 carry/borrow/copy/clear, tape write/shift, skip and reverse-skip rows. Reuse `recordStep_position_digits` and `recordStep_tape_word` for the exact fixed-width source-step fields, and the public layout APIs for all field framing. No rewriting phase A1–A5 is composed by this continuation.
5. Close the live-source endpoint and common ledger with the inherited `RecordRun` composition. Charge every dispatch; restore all work heads and the arbitrary native position/output; erase all scratch tapes globally; preserve the exterior record frame; and prove the time `C*(L+|x|+1)` and radius `C*(L+1)`. The coefficient can be changed if that ledger requires it.

The admission has an explicit `Proof sketch` immediately before it. No missing helper statement was postulated. The target still depends on `sorryAx` directly, not through a newly admitted helper.

## Delivery and replay

The ZIP contains this report, the full modified source at its repository-relative path, the format-patch series against the recorded base, an incremental git bundle with that base as its prerequisite, the final sweep and axiom logs, supporting verification evidence, and `SHA256SUMS`. Only the owned source file is committed. No verification scripts, logs or reports are added to the repository.

On a checkout containing the base, apply `patches/*.patch` with `git am`, or fetch the delivery branch from `fill-s128-C-cont2.bundle`. The bundle and patch are alternate transports of the same commit. Verification/replay logs confirm the bundle prerequisite, patch applicability, and equality of the reconstructed source. Run `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` from the extracted package root.

# §12.8 fill C — continuation 3

**Complete: 1/1.** `Turing.exists_recordStepTM` is proved. No private helper is admitted, and the proved-modulo set is empty. All seven stream-C targets have axiom sets contained in `{propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}`; none contains `sorryAx`.

Base: `635afc668269637e6572698bb1a37d8bd63581e8`, on `complexity/arora-barak-ch3-4`. Working branch: `fill/s128-C-cont3`. Delivery commit: `35fa007145c5d793a80d937e99c6e8d13c3a81e5`.

The required first ancestry check, `git merge-base --is-ancestor 0659a9ab2d6101cc5fbd049d370810f291384230 HEAD`, succeeded before proof work. The base is newer than that ancestor only in the continuation brief and audit evidence; no Lean source changed between them. The inherited admission inventory is exactly the brief's 37 declarations. The second continuation report was read first, followed by the original and continuation briefs, the reports they cite, the workflow/policy, and the binding R8 design route.

This ZIP is the delivery. Nothing was pushed and no PR was created.

## What is proved

The existing four-tape `recordStepMachine` and its single `phaseHostTM` instance are unchanged. The inherited full read and halted-source proof are reused unchanged.

For a live source, the proof now composes the full native cycle, including the empty-input case, complement, normal-branch borrow, saved-position seek, and D cleanup. The native position and output prefix are restored exactly. The observed action agrees with `M.step c` and its output, and its edge test is equivalent to the window condition.

The out-of-window branch invokes the inherited B-clear/reject segment before any record write and restores the whole original configuration except its verdict state.

The successful branch maps the state, performs the exact clamped input-position update on B with copy-back when needed, writes and shifts each work-tape field, maps the tag, and returns through the inverse skips. A local processed-prefix invariant is framed by the public field-layout lemmas. The final patch is exactly the target theorem's interval; every scratch tape is globally blank, all work heads and the native position are restored, and the output is unchanged. Every segment includes the pre-verdict cut and the inclusive head bound.

With `n = x.length`, `W = posWidth n`, `L = (joinFields (cfgRecord s c τ)).length`, and the public seek coefficient `Cseek`, the original common coefficient is retained:

`C = 200 * (k + 3) * (Cseek + 1)`.

The complete run has time at most `C * (L + n + 1)` and work-head radius at most `C * (L + 1)`. The native cycle costs at most `20 * (Cseek + 1) * (W + n + 1)`; successful apply costs at most `40 * (k + 3) * (L + 1)`. The layout span gives `W ≤ L`, so both fit the final ledger.

## New declarations

All twelve declarations are private. There are eleven proved theorems and one specification abbreviation; there are no admissions.

| Declaration | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `recordStep_arithmetic_transport` | One R1 carry/borrow transport on a dedicated digit tape, preserving the rich frame and native data; reused for saved-position borrow and both position-update arithmetic branches. |
| `recordRun_mono` | Widen a `RecordRun` radius before concatenating segments. |
| `recordStep_restore_digits` | Compose I6 complement and the normal-only I7 borrow, obtaining the original native-position digits with the full cut and width bound. |
| `RecordStepSeekSpec` | Package the unchanged complete public input-seek witness contract for reuse at two positions. |
| `recordStep_restore_native` | Compose I6–I9, seek on D/Cs, clear D, and dispatch with exactly restored native position/output and scratch frame. |
| `recordStep_live_native` | Compose I0–I9 for every live source, including empty input, ending at apply with only canonical B digits nonblank. |
| `recordStep_observed_action` | Identify the accumulated transition/output and apply the inherited window equivalence. |
| `recordStep_tape_run` | Compose the two A3 scans: marked write, then mark shift, with the exact applied-action field and framed endpoint. |
| `recordStep_copyback_run` | Copy changed position digits B→F1 and clear B; exact time `4 * w.length + 6`. |
| `recordStep_write_back` | Compose A5's `k + 2` public inverse skips on the completed record, restoring the record head and reaching yes. |
| `recordStep_position_run` | Handle stationary motion, both clamps, and genuine carry/borrow, then copy back if needed and erase B. |
| `recordStep_apply_run` | Compose A1–A5 using the local processed-prefix invariant, including exact record-frame normalization, restored heads, cut, and linear ledger. |

No host, phase family, index family, restriction lemma, or native transition table was added. The inherited `recordStep_restrict` remains the sole restriction-to-digit-bank lemma and is reused through `recordStep_transport`. Probe, Save, and Read and their gap docstrings are unchanged. Carry and borrow consistently use the existing R1 route; no whole-bank plain symbol-lift was substituted.

The new code cites the existing arithmetic/value identities, clear and map specializations, native segments, and `RecordRun`. It uses public scan, copy, clear, skip, inverse-skip, and arithmetic contracts through the inherited `recordStep_phase_run`. No private general field-layout, buffer-map, rewind-heads, counter-layout, or host proof was introduced. The local field facts specialize `fieldsTape_field`, `fieldOffset_succ`, `fieldOffset_add_length_le`, and `length_joinFields_add_one` to the source/final record prefixes.

## Delivery and replay

The archive contains this report, the full owned source under its repository path, `patches/` from `git format-patch` against the base, an incremental git bundle, complete verification logs and probe sources, all four duplication screens, and `SHA256SUMS`. The bundle requires the recorded base commit and carries `refs/heads/fill/s128-C-cont3`.

Checksum validation and replay from the base through `git am` were performed; the replayed tree matches the delivered commit. Replay evidence is in `logs/replay.log`.

To reproduce, apply the patch series to the recorded base, obtain the pinned dependencies with `lake exe cache get`, and run the unchanged checker over the supplied 98-module order in a new `TCSLIB_OLEANS` directory. Run the included probe/axiom files through the same checker with that object tree. No publication or remote write is part of this delivery.
